fix_commit.message: avcodec/libdav1d: fix heap overflow in US ITU-T T.35 metadata parsing
fix_commit.author: Ruikai Peng

findings.title: Unchecked 16-bit read of provider_code in US ITU-T T.35 branch causes heap-buffer-overflow
findings.message: In parse_itut_t35_metadata(), when refactoring the country_code/provider_code dispatch into a switch statement, the read of provider_code for the US (ITU_T_T35_COUNTRY_CODE_US) branch was changed from the bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() to the unchecked bytestream2_get_be16u() variant, with no prior validation that at least 2 bytes remain in the GetByteContext (gb). bytestream2_get_be16u() (see libavcodec/bytestream.h) does not verify bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) before reading, so if the ITU-T T.35 payload has country_code == 0xB5 (US) and a payload shorter than 2 bytes (e.g. 1 byte), the read overruns the end of the payload buffer by up to 2 bytes, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read. The analogous UK country_code path elsewhere in the function already guards this with an explicit bytestream2_get_bytes_left() check before the unchecked read, but the equivalent guard was omitted for the US path in this refactor.
findings.suggestion: Validate the remaining bytes in the GetByteContext before performing the unchecked 16-bit read, matching the pattern already used for the UK country_code branch: check bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < 2 and return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA (or otherwise bail out) before calling bytestream2_get_be16u(). Alternatively, use the bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() variant instead of the 'u' (unchecked) variant.

ground_truth.root_cause: During a refactor that converted the country_code/provider_code dispatch logic in parse_itut_t35_metadata() into nested switch statements, the previously bounds-checked bytestream2_get_be16() call used to read provider_code was replaced by the unchecked bytestream2_get_be16u() variant for the US country_code case, without adding an explicit length check (bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < 2) beforehand. The analogous branch for the UK country code does include such a guard, but it was inconsistently omitted for the US branch, leaving a gap where attacker-controlled short payloads are read out of bounds.
